description.narrative: In collaboration with the African Institute of Investigative Journalism (AIIJ), UNNGOF will conduct training of journalists across the country. The training will equip journalists to be prepared to play key roles in advancing Human Rights throughout the election cycle.

comment.narrative: A total of six meetings were planned, each accommodating 40 participants. Specifically, six regional trainings were to be conducted in Gulu, Mbarara, and Jinja. These trainings were designed to equip participants with practical skills and knowledge on the critical role of media in advancing Human Rights, Democracy, and Elections in Uganda.

The training of journalists was conducted in 2 phases: Phase One:The disaggregation of the 129 journalists trained is as follows:1. Mbarara: 42 participants (10 females, 32 males)2. Gulu: 42 participants (10 females, 32 males)3. Jinja: 45 participants (20 females, 25 males)Phase Two:Reporting covered all three regionsâ€”Western, Acholi, and Busoga sub-regions. comment.narrative: Currently, Uganda is experiencing shrinking space and Human rights violations are on-going, since we arestill within the election cycle.

Despite the impromptu closure of UNNGOF, which led to the shutdown of vital communications channels such as the digital hub and WhatsApp group, significant progress had already been made in strengthening human rights work. Evidence captured at the time shows that several CSOs had proactively conducted digital security trainings for their staff and member organizations. These efforts not only enhanced resilience but also heightened awareness of digital surveillance risks.The collaborative framework developed during the retreat of human rights actors served as a guiding tool for many organizations, enabling more coordinated responses. Reports of human rights violations were systematically documented and submitted, primarily to the police and the Electoral Commission, ensuring accountability mechanisms were engaged.Moreover, the wide-reaching media campaign spearheaded by our strategic partner, Nation Media Group, amplified the visibility of these issues and brought them to national attention. This combination of digital preparedness, collaborative structures, reporting mechanisms, and media advocacy demonstrates the resilience and adaptability of human rights actors, even in the face of institutional setbacks.
